Die Arteria ulnaris ist der medial gelegene Endast der Arteria brachialis in der Fossa cubitalis, verläuft am Unterarm überwiegend ulnarseitig und zieht am Handgelenk oberflächlich des Retinaculum flexorum durch die Canalis ulnaris (Guyon-Loge) in die Hohlhand; sie gibt u. a. die Arteria interossea communis ab und bildet in der Hand vorwiegend den Arcus palmaris superficialis (sowie über den Ramus profundus Beitrag zum Arcus palmaris profundus), zur arteriellen Versorgung der ulnaren Unterarmanteile und der palmaren Hand einschließlich der Arteriae digitales palmares.

Die arteria radialis ist der laterale Endast der arteria brachialis und verläuft an der radialen Unterarmseite zum carpus, zieht in der Hand über die dorsoradiale Region durch die tabatière anatomique und gelangt zwischen den Köpfen des musculus interosseus dorsalis I in die Hohlhand, wo sie den arcus palmaris profundus bildet; sie dient der arteriellen Versorgung v. a. der radialen Unterarm- und Handanteile einschließlich des Daumen-/Zeigefingerbereichs über arteria princeps pollicis und arteria radialis indicis sowie über Anastomosen zum arcus palmaris superficialis.

arcus palmaris superficialis / arcus volaris superficialis

Der arcus palmaris superficialis liegt in der Hohlhand oberflächlich auf den Flexorensehnen und den Lumbricales und wird überwiegend durch die a. ulnaris gebildet; er wird lateral meist durch den ramus palmaris superficialis a. radialis (oder einen ramus palmaris profundus) komplettiert. Aus ihm entspringen die aa. digitales palmares communes, die in die aa. digitales palmares propriae zu den Fingern übergehen. Funktionell dient er der arteriellen Versorgung der oberflächlichen palmarseitigen Hand- und Fingerweichteile.

gemeinsame palmare Fingerarterie / gemeinsame palmare Digitalarterie

Die aa. digitales palmares communes verlaufen in der Hohlhand distalwärts in den Spatien intermetacarpalia oberflächlicher als die mm. interossei palmares und in Nachbarschaft zu den nn. digitales palmares communes; sie entspringen überwiegend aus dem arcus palmaris superficialis, ziehen zu den commissurae interdigitales und teilen sich dort in je zwei aa. digitales palmares propriae zu den benachbarten Fingern. Hauptfunktion ist die arterielle Versorgung der Digiti manus (v. a. palmar) einschließlich der Anteile an Haut, Sehnen und Gelenken der Finger.

Die a. digitalis palmaris propria verläuft an der Palmarseite an den radialen bzw. ulnaren Rändern der Finger (digitale Gefäßnervenstraße) von proximal nach distal; sie entsteht aus der a. digitalis palmaris communis (aus dem arcus palmaris superficialis) und gibt u.a. Äste zur Phalanx proximalis, Phalanx media und Phalanx distalis ab sowie Verbindungen über arcus pulpae. Hauptfunktion ist die arterielle Versorgung der palmar gelegenen Weichteile und Knochen der Finger einschließlich der Fingerbeere und des Endglieds.

desc:
ComprehensiveCadaver is a fully searchable cadaveric-based Anki deck, designed specifically for anatomy practical exams. With over 1,500 hours invested in its creation, it serves as a robust resource featuring over 450 high-quality images, including cadaveric and radiologic pictures sourced from more than 15 popular atlases and references such as Rohen’s Anatomy: A Photographic Atlas and the University of Michigan’s BlueLink. In total, ComprehensiveCadaver contains over 6,000 practice questions and spans a wide range of topics including identification, actions, origins and insertions, innervations, embryology, and more. In contrast to other Anki decks, ComprehensiveCadaver features images that have been completely de-labelled except for the highlighted structure in question. This unique approach employs a custom Image Q/A - 2.0.2 format (“Image Q/A – ComprehensiveCadaver”) instead of traditional Image Occlusions, and answer cards visually highlight and color-code structures for enhanced clarity. For example, if the question card identifies the axillary artery, it will be distinctly highlighted in red on the answer card. Organized hierarchically into subdecks by anatomical region, each card is tagged with its corresponding region (ComprehensiveCadaver::Region::) and question type (ComprehensiveCadaver::QuestionType::) and includes a Keyword field for efficient searching. This design allows users to quickly find cards on specific topics, such as "internal carotid artery" or "ICA." Please be aware that due to its use of copyrighted images, ComprehensiveCadaver will not be available on AnkiHub at this time. It is highly recommended to support the original authors by purchasing the atlases that contributed to this deck. Note: Because this deck uses Image Q/A cards, it does not support dark mode. Sorry!

Structure Lists (.pdf) for each subdeck of ComprehensiveCadaver have been prepared, providing a detailed view of the structures covered in each section. Additionally, a complete list of searchable keywords/phrases (in alphabetical order) is available in this spreadsheet, specifically under the Master List sheet. Every card in ComprehensiveCadaver is tagged with relevant keywords for these structures, enabling comprehensive searches across the entire deck or within specific subdecks. Detailed instructions on how to align the deck with your curriculum using these keywords are provided in the following section.

Thanks to ComprehensiveCadaver's detailed tagging system, which includes anatomical regions, question types, and keywords, the deck can be easily tailored to meet specific curriculum needs. For those with a list of required structures, you can customize your study materials as follows:

  1. Download this spreadsheet and insert your list into column B, starting from cell B13.
  2. Remove any unwanted question types from column C to refine your search criteria.
  3. The search query will automatically be generated in Cell D13. Copy this query.
  4. Paste the query into Anki’s search bar under the Browse tab.
  5. To activate cards for study, select all cards displayed by the search, right-click, and choose "Toggle Suspend". Alternatively, move the selected cards to a new or existing deck by right-clicking and selecting "Change Deck".

ComprehensiveCadaver features over 450 de-labelled images set against a clean, white background, gathered from a variety of sources. The source of each image is noted at the bottom of both question and answer cards, as well as within the Source field. Below is a list of the top 10 most frequently used sources, organized from the most to the least utilized. To support the continuation of such resources and to obtain access to the fully labelled images, please consider purchasing the mentioned atlases. Links for purchase are provided below and in the Source field on every card.

  1. Anatomy: A Photographic Atlas (8th Ed.) - 122 images
  2. Complete Anatomy by Elsevier - 90 images
  3. BlueLink by University of Michigan Medical School - 54 images
  4. Anatomy & Physiology Revealed 4.0 - 28 images
  5. e-Anatomy: The Atlas of Imaging - 26 images
  6. Human Anatomy Color Atlas and Textbook (6th Ed.) - 25 images
  7. All-In-One Anatomy Exam Review: Volumes 1-7 - 12 images
  8. Atlas of Clinical Gross Anatomy (2nd Ed.) - 12 images
  9. Clinical Atlas of Human Anatomy (8th Ed.) - 11 images
  10. NetAnatomy - 11 images

Given the deck’s expansive nature, occasional errors are inevitable. If you encounter any inaccuracies or wish to suggest new content, please submit them through this form. Submissions are accessible for review here.

To keep up to date with ComprehensiveCadaver and future projects, including the forthcoming ComprehensiveNeuroanatomy, follow @MarkAAbbott1 on X (formerly Twitter) or MarkAAbbott1 on Reddit.

It is important to recognize that ComprehensiveCadaver, while comprehensive, is not a substitute for hands-on experience in an anatomy lab when available. The deck is designed to supplement, not replace, the rich learning experience of direct cadaver examination. Additionally, it may not cover all anatomical variations or clinical correlations, and you are encouraged to consult additional resources for a more holistic understanding. Finally, this deck is purely educational and isn't a licensed product. I do not claim ownership over any character, text, or image. Any copyrighted material belongs to its respective owner. Use copyrighted images at your discretion. As per Section 107 of the Copyright Act 1976, this deck falls under "fair use" for educational purposes. Any potential infringement is unintentional.
